learn: The package layer's own evidence rules pointed me at the client's parked DOM: the camp keeps a display:none copy of its rule list, so a DOM query or a scripted .click() can operate a hidden, stale editor while the visible screen is elsewhere. Any rater who clicks by text or selector should assert visibility (getBoundingClientRect + elementFromPoint) before concluding that an interaction worked or failed.

One rater cannot close the loop on the rule editor from outside: threshold-value taps are the one interaction I could not verify end to end (six attempts, always with engine.exportRules() as the check). A hands-on rater with a visible-only driver, or a QA transcript of the exact tap path, is the right follow-up before this build ships - the rule layer is the game's whole lever.

Frame time is cheap to measure in the rater's own window (a rAF sample via page.evaluate) and is stronger evidence than a screenshot for motion and polish; the phone walk's screenshots were pixel-bound enough that I did not try to read fps off them.
